children.title: Introduction
children.description: Welcome to the Creatures 3 Web Rebuild documentation

children.title: Norns, Grendels and Ettins
children.description: What actually differs between the three species — genome-by-genome comparison of the stock norn, grendel and ettin: identity plumbing, the shared brain, birth chemistry, the reaction that turns norn-scent into grendel anger, the missing ettin anger organ, species-only stimuli and instincts, ageing under stress, and the breeds shipped in the asset packs

children.title: Age and Lifecycle
children.description: The biochemistry-driven ageing system — Chemical 125 (Life), seven life stages, ageing loci, gene expression timing, consciousness states, birth, death sequence, and state machine transitions

children.title: Overview
children.description: High-level introduction to the Creatures brain architecture adapted from Alan Zucconi's article — covers the original Creatures 1 neural network with 952 neurons and 9 lobes, the Winner Takes All decision mechanism, the Concept lobe situation encoding, and the reinforcement/atrophy/migration learning system

children.title: Brain & Neural Networks
children.description: Neural network architecture, lobes, neurons, and decision making

children.title: [visn] Vision Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the vision lobe connection to SensoryFaculty, neuron layout, input normalization, and downstream tract propagation

children.title: [elvn] Elevation Lobe Architecture
children.description: The planned but never completed Y-axis counterpart to the vision lobe — engine writes to it every tick, but no genome defines it and all data is silently discarded into a dummy lobe

children.title: [detl] Detail Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the detail lobe (detl) — a latent-capacity input lobe with 16 genome-defined neurons (11 engine-written) encoding properties of the IT agent including nearness, carry state, family relationships, size, smell, and motion, with zero tracts in the standard norn genome making it a ready-to-wire substrate for genome evolution

children.title: [situ] Situation Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the situation lobe (situ) — 9 neurons encoding the creature's own state including age, carrying, falling, proximity to mates, music, and player selection

children.title: [driv] Drive Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the drive lobe (driv) — 20 neurons bridging biochemistry and neural networks, encoding motivational states from pain and hunger to social and navigation drives

children.title: [driv→driv] Drive Inhibition Tracts
children.description: Deep-dive into the two driv→driv self-loop tracts (idx 25 and 27 in the standard genome) — the inhibitory mechanism whereby the navigation drives (Up, Down, Exit, Enter, Wait) suppress every biological drive at the brain layer when their signal exceeds 0.1008. Walks through the shared SVRule (LOAD_ACC INPUT[0]; IF_GREATER_THAN 0.1008; BLANK NEURON[0]; STOP), the per-tick timing inside Brain.updateComponents, and uses the lift script (Lifts.cos stim writ targ 75 0) as a concrete end-to-end example showing how a single lift activation produces a ~26 second decision freeze where the creature stares at the lift instead of acting on hunger or other biological drives

children.title: [attn] Attention Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the attention lobe (attn) — the output lobe where 40 category neurons compete via winner-takes-all to select the creature's focus of attention. Includes the complete genome-defined tract architecture showing the three-layer pipeline: sensory inputs (visn, smel, move, noun) feed through the stimulus lobe (stim), which combines with drives (driv), verbs (verb), and friend/foe (forf) in the combination lobe (comb), before projecting to attention via comb→attn

children.title: [decn] Decision Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the decision lobe (decn) — the output lobe where neural competition selects one of 14 voluntary actions via winner-takes-all, driving the creature's motor behavior through the verb-to-decision pipeline and neuron-to-script mapping

children.title: [forf] Friend-or-Foe Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the friend-or-foe lobe (forf) — per-individual relationship tracking with kinship-based initialization, per-tick visibility updates, interaction flagging, dendrite migration, and opinion output for linguistic expression

children.title: [move] Move Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the move lobe (move) — a genome-defined intermediate processing lobe that detects visual motion by computing rate of change of vision displacement, accumulating signals via leaky integration, and gating output to the stimulus source lobe

children.title: [comb] Combination Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the combination lobe (comb) — the central 440-neuron decision matrix (40 categories x 11 actions) where drives, verbs, stimuli, and social relationships converge through 6 inbound tracts, with reinforcement learning on dendrite weights and dual output to attention and decision lobes

children.title: [stim] Stimulus Source Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the stimulus source lobe (stim) — the uniquely catalogued sensory integration layer that aggregates vision proximity, motion detection, smell, and language into a per-category saliency map through 4 inbound tracts, with multiplicative output modulation to the combination lobe

children.title: [noun] Noun Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the noun lobe (noun) — the input mirror for the attention lobe, receiving linguistic, stimulus, and instinct signals that bias which of 40 agent categories the creature will focus on, with a gated outbound tract to the stimulus source lobe

children.title: [verb] Verb Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the verb lobe (verb) — the input mirror for the decision lobe, receiving linguistic, stimulus, and instinct signals that bias which of 13 actions the creature will perform, with dual outbound tracts: row activation into the combination lobe and a direct bypass to the decision lobe for special actions

children.title: [resp] Response Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the response lobe (resp) — the brain's reinforcement learning signal pathway with 20 neurons (one per drive), encoding drive-change consequences from actions via instinct reinforcement and stimulus training, with inbound decision context from decn and outbound drive modulation to driv THIRD_VAR

children.title: [mood] Mood Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the mood lobe (mood) — a single-neuron genome-only aggregation lobe that computes emotional valence from 4 social/threat drives (scared, angry, lonely, friendly) with temporal smoothing, broadcasting the result to all friend-or-foe neurons when mood exceeds a 0.5 threshold

children.title: [smel] Smell Lobe Architecture
children.description: Deep-dive into the smell lobe (smel) — the brain's interface to the Cellular Automata (CA) environmental system with 40 neurons (one per agent category), encoding diffused chemical presence from room CA properties via SensoryFaculty and Instinct, with cross-modal mutual reinforcement with vision and downstream gating to the stimulus source lobe

children.title: Reinforcement Learning Pipeline
children.description: Complete end-to-end reinforcement learning pipeline — from STIM commands through SensoryFaculty stimulus processing, synchronous learning gates, resp lobe signal propagation, reward/punishment chemical-driven dendrite weight modification, and STW/LTW weight consolidation. Covers all three learning modes: stimulus learning (awake), instinct processing (dreaming), and proximal reinforcement (asleep)

children.title: Dendrite Migration
children.description: How the brain reuses synaptic capacity by rewiring weak dendrites onto neurons calling for new connections via Nerve Growth Factor (NGF). Covers the per-tract migration flag, weak-dendrite detection via the strength variable, NGF-driven source and destination neuron selection, weight reset on rewiring, interaction with STW/LTW reinforcement, the friend-or-foe lobe case study, and observable gameplay effects such as habit decay and per-individual relationship learning

children.title: Non-Plastic Dendrites
children.description: Why most tracts in the standard norn brain display all-zero dendrite weight columns — the distinction between plastic (learning) tracts that read/write DENDRITE_CODE in their SVRule and non-plastic (fixed-function) tracts that route signal through a straight-line transform with inert weight slots. Covers the three plasticity paths (SVRule, reward/punishment, migration), the visn->stim case study, a full plasticity table for the 29 standard tracts, how to read the Debugger's PLASTIC/NON-PLASTIC badge and its SVRule-only limitation, and modding implications

children.title: Drive Lobe Periodic Clearing: Instinct Processing & Knowledge Building
children.description: Why the drive lobe periodically zeros every neuron and then rebuilds — traces the Brain.ClearActivity path, the myInstinctsAreBeingProcessed flag, the dreamingState transition, the CAOS DREA pulses issued by the sleepy/tired decision script, and the knowledge-building loop that refreshes myAssistanceKnowledge for linguistic teaching

children.title: Brain Chemicals (1-9)
children.description: Deep-dive into chemistry indices 198-206 — the contiguous 'brain chemical' block reserved for brain-to-body signalling. Covers per-chemical production (stimulus genes, drive system, CAOS), consumption (SVRule CHEMICAL_CODE operand vs per-tract reward/punishment system), the driv->comb init rule that is the sole consumer of Brain chemical 1, Reward, and Punishment in the stock genome, the navigation drives Up/Down/Exit/Enter/Wait, and JS rebuild alignment with debugging checklist

children.title: Combining Multiple Input Signals at a Neuron
children.description: How incoming signals from multiple dendrites are combined into a single scalar at the destination neuron. Covers the two-stage pipeline: tract SVRules accumulating into dst.state[1] via opcodes 50/51 with per-add saturation, and lobe SVRules reading that scalar as neuron[1]. Explains why the combination is order-dependent and non-associative, why cross-lobe per-source contributions are unrecoverable, and how to interpret the Inspector's SVRule trace tooltip.

children.title: Brain → IT Object Pipeline
children.description: How the creature's attention target (IT) is determined through the three-layer pipeline: SensoryFaculty perception, brain attention lobe competition, and MotorFaculty agent selection with visual validation

children.title: Instinct System
children.description: Hardwired behaviour patterns encoded as G_INSTINCT genome genes — the complete lifecycle from genome storage through age-filtered queue loading, REM sleep processing with two-pass stimulation and reinforcement, chemical signalling (212/213) for STW/LTW learning mode switching, destructive queue consumption, and post-instinct knowledge extraction for creature-to-creature teaching

children.title: Creature Sleep
children.description: The multi-phase sleep process — LifeFaculty state machine (alert/asleep/dreaming), CAOS script orchestration of the sleep cycle, falling asleep via involuntary action, the dream loop with DREA 1 triggering instinct processing, chemical signalling (212/213) for STW/LTW learning mode, knowledge building phase after instincts, waking conditions based on sleepiness/tiredness drives, state transition safety rules, and the asleep locus biochemistry interface

children.title: Zombie State
children.description: The zombie life state — alive but brain-disconnected. Engine semantics (motor frozen, eyes open, hearing intact, pose 58 forced), the SetWhetherZombie rules (dead-immune, un-zombify always returns to alert, locked transitions), the hand-holding flow, and the four bootstrap CAOS scripts that drive creatures into zombie state during gameplay (Lifts.cos lift rides, gene pod.cos splicing, GUI 1.cos teleport-import, creatureDoneTo.cos pointer-release safety net)

children.title: Stimulus System
children.description: The bridge between world events and creature brains — stimulus definitions, delivery types (WRIT/SHOU/SIGN/TACT), perception checks, the three processing macros (ORDR/URGE/SWAY), brain lobe wiring, chemical injection, and reinforcement learning

children.title: Creature Faculties
children.description: The 9 specialized subsystems that control creature behavior

children.title: Brain Faculty
children.description: The creature's central decision-making system — dual-mode neural network with instinct processing during REM sleep, knowledge extraction for creature-to-creature teaching, bidirectional biochemistry coupling via chemical pointers and neuron loci, SVRule algebraic computation engine, and the Vat Kit debug interface

children.title: Sensory Faculty
children.description: The creature's perceptual gateway — vision, smell, stimulus processing, category representatives, friend/foe social memory, and the reinforcement learning system

children.title: Motor Faculty
children.description: The creature's action execution system — brain decision pipeline, IT object management, voluntary and involuntary script firing, URGE override system, and biochemistry locus binding

children.title: Linguistic Faculty
children.description: The creature's language and communication system — vocabulary learning with three-stage pronunciation, speech generation (SayWhatDoing, ExpressNeed, ExpressOpinion), sentence parsing with 30+ syntax patterns, social intelligence for command filtering, inter-creature conversation, and brain noun/verb nudging

children.title: Vision System
children.description: The engine-side vision pipeline — world scanning, category representative selection with 5 algorithms, brain input writing (visn/elvn), and VM stability

children.title: Hearing System
children.description: The engine-side hearing pipeline — no dedicated brain lobe, range-based CanHear() gating on SHOU stimuli, speech processing through LinguisticFaculty, name-based wake-up, and crowding score

children.title: Touch System
children.description: The engine-side touch pipeline — no dedicated brain lobe, AABB bounding box overlap via CanTouch() gating on TACT stimuli, creature reach animation via ReachOut(), and agent manager touch queries

children.title: Reproductive Faculty
children.description: The creature's breeding system — hysteresis-based fertility control, biochemistry-driven ovulation cycles, sperm donation and probabilistic fertilisation, genetic crossover with mutation, multiple births (twins/triplets), pregnancy visualisation via progesterone, and egg-laying through the involuntary action pipeline

children.title: Egg Hatching
children.description: End-to-end documentation of the egg hatching pipeline — eggs are simple bootstrap-script agents (classifiers 3 4 1 / 3 4 0) driven entirely by CAOS, the engine-side per-tick TICK timer that fires their state machine, the pose-progression ripening from laying through cracking to BORN, the Hatchery (incubator) fast path, c3_max_norns / c3_max_creatures population caps, and how timeScale acceleration affects hatch time

children.title: Music Faculty
children.description: The creature's interface to the dynamic music system — stateless mood calculation from 14 weighted drives, fear-based threat level, Norn-only selectability gating, hatching detection, brain situation lobe integration, and MusicManager aggregation pipeline

children.title: Expressive Faculty
children.description: The creature's facial expression system — genome-defined drive-to-expression weightings, winner-takes-all expression selection with 0.5-centred scoring, smooth transitions through neutral state, sleepiness-driven blinking, eye state control, ear set mapping, and CAOS FACE/EXPR commands

children.title: Life Faculty
children.description: Faculty 8 — the life cycle, the consciousness states and death: the seven stages and the Life-chemical thresholds that advance them, the six-state consciousness enum and its transition rules, the three routes to death and the seven-step death sequence, the genome's three death receptors (ATP, Energy, chemical 90), and how to read the health and death-risk indicators

children.title: Creature Behavior Scripts
children.description: Complete reference of the CAOS scripts that implement creature behaviors — voluntary decisions (approach, eat, hit, rest, travel), involuntary reflexes (flinch, sneeze, shiver, sleep, death), creature-to-creature interactions (slap, mate), and done-to reactions (patted, slapped, collision), including the stimulus feedback loop that drives reinforcement learning

children.title: Creature Perception
children.description: How creatures see, smell, hear, and perceive their world

children.title: Movement Decision Chain
children.description: Complete chain of mechanisms from biochemistry through brain decisions, MotorFaculty gating, CAOS script execution, skeleton animation, and map physics that determines if and how a creature moves

children.title: Gaits
children.description: What a creature's gait is, how the animation string and pose system work, how the genome defines up to 16 walking animations, and how biochemistry-driven receptor loci pick which one plays on each WALK command

children.title: Gait Selection System
children.description: How biochemistry-driven gait loci compete across 16 slots to select walking animations, from genome receptor wiring through chemical competition to skeleton animation playback

children.title: Drive System: From Chemical to Decision
children.description: End-to-end walkthrough of how a bloodstream chemical becomes a drive, travels through a receptor into the Creature's drive loci, and is pushed into the brain's drive lobe each tick — traced with the Hunger for carbohydrate example

children.title: Creature Action Pipeline
children.description: The multi-stage pipeline from biochemistry drives through brain neural lobes into the MotorFaculty, which fires the appropriate CAOS decision script to execute creature actions

children.title: Creature Decisions Script
children.description: How creatureDecisions.cos defines CAOS scripts for each brain decision — action validation, execution, and Disappoint stimulus for failed actions

children.title: Creature Eating: From Action to Biochemistry
children.description: Complete pipeline from brain eat decision through CAOS script execution, stimulus delivery, chemical injection, organ reactions, and drive reduction feedback loop

children.title: Pat and Slap: Teaching Through Touch
children.description: End-to-end pipeline for patting and slapping a creature — pointer click, body-part detection, creatureDoneTo.cos scripts, STIM WRIT stimulus dispatch, genome chemical injection, and reinforcement lobe training

children.title: Air and Breathing: How Creatures Suffocate
children.description: How creatures sense air — a per-tick geometric test of the head's room type against WATER_ROOM_TYPE_1/2 that sets myAirQualityLocus, how that locus feeds chemical 29 (Air) and the drowning chemical through genome emitters and receptors, and how this leads to death via LifeFaculty

children.title: Biochemistry System
children.description: Complete biochemistry architecture including chemicals, organs, reactions, and loci

children.title: Energy and Metabolism
children.description: The complete energy chain from food intake through chemical conversion to organ function — ATP consumption, organ damage/repair, life force, organ failure, and the death spiral

children.title: Chemicals
children.description: What chemicals are in a creature's bloodstream — their in-game characteristics (ID, name, concentration, half-life, starting level), how they are produced, transformed and consumed by emitters, reactions and receptors, the main families of chemical (metabolites, drives, hormones, pheromones, neurotransmitters, injury/toxin signals, immune chemicals, pharmaceuticals, the Life ageing clock), and their role in health, emotion, learning, reproduction, ageing and world interaction

children.title: Neuroemitters
children.description: The one-way bridge from a creature's brain to its biochemistry — how a neuroemitter watches up to three brain neurons, multiplies their activity to form a biological AND-gate, and injects up to four chemicals into the bloodstream when they all agree. Includes a full walkthrough of the only neuroemitter in the standard Norn genome: the hard-wired grendel fear reflex that releases Adrenalin, Fear and Crowded when a Norn sees a grendel moving in its visual field.

children.title: Organ to Real-Life Mapping
children.description: Maps each of the 21 creature organs to a real-life biological equivalent (liver, pancreas, lungs, hypothalamus, gonads, adrenal gland, etc.) based on the reactions, receptors and emitters genetically assigned to each organ in the Norn genome

children.title: Organ #0 — Hidden Body Organ ("Brain")
children.description: Detailed reference for Organ #0 — the implicit body organ created at birth with no organ gene. Covers its creation in Biochemistry.initFromGenome, default parameters, role as a fallback container for orphan biochemistry genes, implicit ATP→ADP drain, participation in life-force decay / injury / repair, and why it is labelled "Brain" in the debugger

children.title: Organ #1 — Hypothalamus / Limbic System
children.description: In-game role of Organ #1 — the creature's drive and emotion hub. Converts drive-backup reservoirs into felt drives (pain, hunger, cold, heat, tiredness, loneliness), manages the Fear ↔ Anger mood circuit with adrenalin amplification, broadcasts stress hormones, and emits pheromones, libido suppressant, progesterone, boredom and air signals

children.title: Organ #2 — Liver (with Immune, Kidney and Detox)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #2 — the creature's central chemical workshop. Combines liver, kidney, immune and pharmacological functions: builds and recycles muscle, handles the urea cycle, thermoregulates via sweating, gates sleep, drains felt drives, produces antibodies against each antigen, and breaks down alcohol, poisons and drugs

children.title: Organ #3 — Pancreas (β-cells / Insulin)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #3 — the creature's long-term energy-storage regulator. Converts excess Glucose into Glycogen reserves, regulates itself from the creature's current Adipose Tissue level, and emits Loneliness when the creature is alone

children.title: Organ #4 — Pancreas (α-cells / Glucagon)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #4 — the creature's fuel-release valve and sleep-hormone source. Breaks Glycogen back into Glucose so the body can spend its reserves, has a Hotness-modulated clock rate, and emits Sleepase from a sleep brain neuron so the creature can actually fall asleep

children.title: Organ #5 — Pineal Gland
children.description: In-game role of Organ #5 — the creature's sleep-maintenance organ. Releases Sleepase while the creature is asleep so it stays asleep, slowly drains the loneliness drive back into its reservoir, and links subtly to Hunger for fat through a circulatory signal

children.title: Organ #6 — Small Intestine (Lipase)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #6 — the creature's fat-digestion organ. Breaks dietary Fat into three Triglycerides plus Cholesterol, regulates its own speed from the current Fatty Acid level, and broadcasts a small Stress signal while working

children.title: Organ #7 — Salivary Glands / Pancreatic Amylase
children.description: In-game role of Organ #7 — the creature's carbohydrate-digestion organ. Turns dietary Starch into four units of Glucose, regulates its pace from the current Fatty Acid level, and broadcasts a small Stress signal while working

children.title: Organ #8 — Adipose Tissue (Lipogenesis)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #8 — the creature's fat-storage organ. Compacts circulating Triglycerides into Adipose Tissue at an 8:1 ratio, self-regulates from the current Pyruvate level, and broadcasts a small Stress signal while working

children.title: Organ #9 — Adipose Tissue (Lipolysis)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #9 — the creature's fat-reserve release organ. Breaks Adipose Tissue back into eight units of Triglyceride so the body can burn its stored fat, self-regulates from the current Glucose level, and broadcasts a small Stress signal while working

children.title: Organ #10 — Jejunum / Fat Appetite Sensor
children.description: In-game role of Organ #10 — the creature's final fat-digestion step and fat-appetite source. Breaks Triglycerides into three Fatty Acids so they can be burned, paces itself with the current Pyruvate level, and continuously emits the Hunger for fat drive that pushes a Norn to seek fatty food

children.title: Organ #11 — Skeletal Muscle (Fatigue Sensor)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #11 — the creature's tiredness-recovery organ. Drains felt Tiredness back into its reservoir so rest and sleep actually help, gates recovery on the current Energy level, and broadcasts a small Stress signal while working

children.title: Organ #12 — Skeletal Muscle (Glycolysis)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #12 — the creature's primary energy engine. Converts Glucose + ADP into Pyruvate + ATP to power movement, paces itself with the current Amino Acid level, and emits Anabolic Steroid toward the muscles so activity builds strength

children.title: Organ #13 — Liver (Gluconeogenesis)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #13 — the creature's emergency sugar factory. Rebuilds Glucose from Pyruvate + ATP so a starving Norn still has a trickle of blood sugar, paces itself with the current Amino Acid level, and emits the Hunger for protein drive that makes exerted creatures seek meat and cheese

children.title: Organ #14 — Stomach (Pepsin)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #14 — the creature's protein-digestion organ. Turns dietary Protein into four units of Amino Acid, paces itself from the current Triglyceride level, and broadcasts a small Stress signal while working

children.title: Organ #15 — Gonads (Testes / Ovaries)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #15 — the creature's reproductive hormone factory. Emits Testosterone, Oestrogen and Arousal Potential when fertile, generates the Hunger for carbohydrate drive, opens Crowded / Boredom / Sex drive from their backups and drains carb, fat and coldness drives back, is modulated by Pain and Fear, and produces several flavoured Stress signals

children.title: Organ #16 — Adipocytes (de novo Lipogenesis)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #16 — the creature's "sugar to fat" organ. Builds fresh Fatty Acids from excess Pyruvate and ATP so a carbohydrate-rich diet can still produce body fat, paces itself with available ATP, and continuously emits the Hunger for protein drive

children.title: Organ #17 — Mitochondria (β-Oxidation)
children.description: In-game role of Organ #17 — the creature's fat-burning engine. Turns Fatty Acid + ADP into Pyruvate + ATP so body fat becomes real energy, also repackages surplus fatty acids into triglycerides, drains felt Hotness back to its reservoir, and emits the Crowded drive plus two Stress channels

children.title: Organ #18 — Uterus
children.description: In-game role of Organ #18 — the creature's pregnancy organ. Emits a steady Comfort signal while the creature is pregnant, keeping a gestating Norn visibly calm and content, and tunes that signal subtly to the mother's pyruvate-based energy state

children.title: Organ #19 — Adrenal Gland
children.description: In-game role of Organ #19 — the creature's fight-or-flight energy burst. Combines Glycogen with Adrenalin to flood the body with 8× Glucose when the hypothalamus releases adrenalin in response to stress, is tuned by the creature's protein hunger, and emits Upatrophin while moving uphill so climbing costs real energy

children.title: Organ #20 — Lungs
children.description: In-game role of Organ #20 — the creature's oxygen-burning engine. Combines Pyruvate with Oxygen into six units of Energy and CO₂ (the creature's largest energy release), scales its clock rate from the current Oxygen level (so suffocation stalls it), and continuously emits the Sleepiness drive that makes every Norn gradually need to sleep
